subject: Private cluster cutover runbook and storage hardening
messages:
From: Ben Lawrence <ben@ironwood.io>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@ironwood.io>
Date: 2027-06-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: private cluster cutover — runbook ask

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for walking us through the architecture yesterday. We want to lock a proposed cutover window for our on-prem cluster (no VPC peering, direct transit) and get a concrete runbook we can follow during the site outage. Two items we especially need covered:

- control-plane HA steps (leader election failover expectations)
- storage key-handling for encrypted blockstore (we manage KMS on-prem)

Can your team send a runbook draft and a short checklist we can run during the maintenance window next month? Prefer a weekday evening window.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Lawrence
Director, Platform Engineering
Ironwood Health
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Ben Lawrence <ben@ironwood.io>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: private cluster cutover — runbook ask

Ben —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass runbook (ironsite-cutover-runbook-draft-v1.pdf) and a lightweight checklist. High-level notes up front:

- Proposed maintenance windows: Tue or Wed 1900–2300 local (we prefer Tue 1900–2300 PST to give ops staff daytime prep).
- Cutover scope: upgrade control-plane to HA (3 etcd + 3 control-plane), drain and replace worker nodepools for tenant/worker separation, perform PV unbind/rehydrate tests for blockstore, and rotate KMS keys for blockstore encryption.
- Rollback guardrails: automated canary rollback if API latency exceeds 250ms for >5 minutes, immediate rollback option to previous snapshot for blockstore if integrity checks fail.

Key items in the runbook (short):
1) Pre-checks (monitoring healthy, k8s versions, etcd quorum snapshot current).
2) Control-plane switchover steps (cordon older control-plane, bring up new control-plane nodes behind LB, validate pod scheduling).
3) Storage actions (snapshot PVs, copy snapshots to staging host, new key injection test).
4) Nodepool replacement plan (drain, cordon, create new nodes with required taints/labels, NVMe ephemeral cache config).
5) Post-cutover validation (token latency suite, KV hit-ratio, storage IO smoke tests).

Two asks from your side to make the runbook authoritative:
- Confirm we have on-prem KMS endpoints and who has access to rotate keys (ops@ironwood.io).
- Confirm allowed outage window and whether we should bring in your on-call DB team during the storage snapshot step.

Attached: ironsite-cutover-runbook-draft-v1.pdf (runbook), storage-kms-mapping.xlsx (KMS endpoints placeholder).

I'll loop in Aditya and Karthik below for storage and nodepool specifics.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, Ben Lawrence <ben@ironwood.io>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-27T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: private cluster cutover — runbook ask

Ben / team —

Quick follow-up on storage and node pool labeling:

- KMS: For customer-managed KMS we recommend a dual-key model: a site-level envelope key + per-PV data keys. During cutover we only rotate the envelope keys (fast) and validate unlock using a small sample of PVs. Full re-encryption is a separate, scheduled operation.
- Node pools: plan for three worker tiers: gpu (taint: workload=gpu:NoSchedule), shared (no taint, default), and io-heavy (label: io=high, uses local NVMe ephemeral for cache). Keep the io-heavy pool in a different failure domain (different racks) to reduce correlated failures.
- PV handling: snapshot, mount read-only on a staging host, run checksum verification, then rebind. If checksum mismatch, halt and escalate to ops@ironwood.io.

I added a short appendix to the runbook PDF with the KMS mapping table and suggested kubectl commands for snapshot/restore.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Ben Lawrence <ben@ironwood.io>
Date: 2027-06-27T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: private cluster cutover — runbook ask

Ben —

A few operational checks from infra/runtime side:

- Kernel tuning: confirm vm.swappiness and low-latency sched settings on worker nodes prior to enabling NVMe cache. We'll push a daemonset that verifies and fixes sysctl on boot; add this to pre-checks.
- NVMe wear-leveling: ephemeral caching should be configured with strict TTL and periodic rehydrate to avoid long-lived dirty caches; advise a cache eviction policy and a scheduled scrub during low-traffic windows.
- Networking: because this is a VPC-less topology, ensure the external LB has health-checks on both control-plane and API LB ports and that BGP sessions (where used) are stable. We'll include a curl-based API check in post-cutover validation.

I'll attach the tiny script we'll run for API health checks to the Drive link (under related_links). Also recommend a dry-run in staging with 10% of traffic routed to the new cluster to validate canary metrics.

— Aditya
